items.front: Later Vedic period dates and defining geographic shift?
items.back: c. 1000–600 BCE; Aryans expand eastward from Sapta-Sindhu into the Gangetic plains.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Contents of the Sama, Yajur and Atharva Vedas?
items.back: Sama = chants/melodies; Yajur = sacrificial formulae; Atharva = charms, spells and remedies.
items.examPoint: Contents of the three Vedas (Sama chants, Yajur formulae, Atharva charms)
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Textual layers attached to each Veda, ritual → philosophy?
items.back: Samhita → Brahmana (ritual commentary) → Aranyaka (forest books) → Upanishad (philosophy).
items.examPoint: Later Vedic literature — Sama/Yajur/Atharva Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Later Vedic word for iron, and what it enabled?
items.back: Krishna Ayas ('black metal'); iron tools cleared dense Gangetic forests for extensive agriculture.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Signature pottery of the Later Vedic period?
items.back: Painted Grey Ware (PGW); Black-and-Red Ware also used.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: New royal titles reflecting hereditary, expansive kingship?
items.back: Samrat (universal ruler) and Chakravartin (emperor); king cast as protector of Dharma.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: New Later Vedic office reflecting revenue collection?
items.back: Sangrahitri (treasurer); alongside Purohita (priest), Senani (army), Gramini (village), Ratnins (nobles).
items.examPoint: Administrative officials (Purohita, Senani, Gramini, Sangrahitri, Ratnin)
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: What happened to the Sabha and Samiti in the Later Vedic period?
items.back: They lost importance and became largely ceremonial as kingship centralised.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: The three great royal sacrifices and their purpose?
items.back: Rajasuya (royal consecration), Ashvamedha (horse — assert dominance), Vajapeya (Kshatriya superiority).
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Ashrama system — the four life-stages in order?
items.back: Brahmacharya → Grihastha → Vanaprastha → Sannyasa (mainly upper-caste males).
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Gotra rule in the Later Vedic period?
items.back: Gotra inherited from the father (patrilineal); marriage within the same gotra was forbidden.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Which deities rose as Indra/Agni/Varuna receded?
items.back: Vishnu and Rudra (Shiva) rose; dharma and karma grew important.
items.examPoint: Shift of deities (Vishnu & Rudra); dharma & karma
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Upanishads: Brahman vs Atman; early currency token?
items.back: Brahman = universal reality, Atman = individual soul (plus karma, moksha). Early token: nishka; barter still dominant.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period

items.front: Sources of the Later Vedic period, and the basic economic shift?
items.back: Sama, Yajur and Atharva Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads; mobile pastoralism gave way to settled agriculture.
items.examPoint: Later Vedic literature — Sama/Yajur/Atharva Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: How did the Later Vedic period end (c. 600 BCE)?
items.back: It gave way to the sixteen Mahajanapadas and the second urbanisation; Magadha rose under Bimbisara and Ajatashatru.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Centre of Later Vedic culture?
items.back: Kuru–Panchala, the upper Ganga–Yamuna doab.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Origin of the word 'Aryan', and when did Bhakti arise?
items.back: From the Sanskrit 'Arya' — the people were named after their language; Bhakti arose only in the 7th–8th century AD.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Who held the Indian theory of the Aryan homeland?
items.back: Sampurnanand and A. C. Das (Sapta Sindhu); Ganganath Jha (Brahmarshi Desh); Laxmidhar Shastri (foot of the Himalayas).
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: How many Upanishads by tradition, which is the oldest, and what are they called?
items.back: 108; the Brihadaranyaka is the oldest and largest; they are called Vedanta.
items.examPoint: Upanishads/Brahmanas exam facts (parables, pre-Puranic, Satyameva Jayate=Mundaka, Satapatha=Yajurveda, Ekrat/Virat titles, untouchability)
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Which Upanishad has 'Tat tvam asi', taught by Uddalaka to Svetaketu?
items.back: The Chandogya Upanishad.
items.examPoint: Upanishads/Brahmanas exam facts (parables, pre-Puranic, Satyameva Jayate=Mundaka, Satapatha=Yajurveda, Ekrat/Virat titles, untouchability)
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Language and literature at the close of the period?
items.back: Vedic Sanskrit gave way to refined Sanskrit; the Sutras were composed.
items.examPoint: Later Vedic literature — Sama/Yajur/Atharva Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Later Vedic army, and two key PGW–iron sites?
items.back: Iron weapons; horse-drawn chariots, archers and foot soldiers. Sites: Hastinapur and Atranjikhera (UP).
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: The Later Vedic king's image, extra titles, and what replaced kinship?
items.back: Protector of Dharma likened to the gods; titles Ekrat, Virat, Bhoja; territorial control — the word 'Rashtra' appears.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: What did the Janapadas become, and which states were Gana-sanghas?
items.back: Janapadas grew into Mahajanapadas; Vajji and Malla were republics (Gana-sanghas).
items.examPoint: Mahajanapadas — monarchies vs republics, capitals & Magadha's rise
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Capital of Magadha, and three major urban hubs?
items.back: Rajagriha (later Pataliputra); hubs Varanasi, Rajagriha and Ujjayini.
items.examPoint: Mahajanapadas — monarchies vs republics, capitals & Magadha's rise
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Later Vedic Sabha vs Samiti, and who held judicial power?
items.back: Sabha = council of the elite; Samiti = general assembly; the king held judicial authority (the Sabha kept some legal role).
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Effect of royal rituals on the Brahmins; position of the Shudras?
items.back: Brahmins became custodians of religious knowledge with the highest status; Shudras served the other three Varnas with limited rights.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: To whom did the Ashrama scheme apply, and what social evil began?
items.back: Mainly upper-caste males; untouchability began to emerge.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Signs of women's decline, and how was education given?
items.back: Child marriage in some sections; the Aitareya Brahmana calls a daughter a source of misery. Education was oral, in Gurukulas, to Brahmacharis.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: God of the Shudras, the new doctrine of rebirth, and what Upanishadic thought led to?
items.back: Pushan (guardian of cattle); transmigration (rebirth); it set the stage for Jainism and Buddhism.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Irrigation and the measure of wealth in the Later Vedic age?
items.back: Irrigation was limited but growing; cattle remained the main measure of wealth (horses valued for war).
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Later Vedic exchange: tokens, units, merchants, coins and routes?
items.back: Barter with Nishka tokens; Satamana/Krishnala units; 'shreshthin' = chief merchant; coinage only at the end; routes to Central Asia.
items.source: APPSC GK — Later Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)
